Patchcord uses the following open-source libraries, each under the
GNU Lesser General Public License, version 2.1 (full texts alongside this file).

libmtp 1.1.23   https://github.com/libmtp/libmtp  (libmtp-COPYING.txt, libmtp-AUTHORS.txt)
libusb 1.0.30   https://github.com/libusb/libusb  (libusb-COPYING.txt, libusb-AUTHORS.txt)

Both are dynamically linked and live in Patchcord.app/Contents/Frameworks.
You may replace them with your own builds (re-sign the app ad hoc afterwards:
codesign --force --deep --sign - Patchcord.app).

libusb is unmodified.

libmtp is modified. The changes are in libmtp-ct10.patch, which applies with
`patch -p1` to the libmtp-1.1.23 release tarball:
  - Activo CT10 device entry with a new DEVICE_FLAG_NO_USB_RESET (a USB reset
    leaves the CT10 unable to open a new session until replugged).
  - Cancelling an upload now waits 1 s for the device to process the cancel
    and completes the pending bulk read, instead of stalling the next command
    for ~60 s.
  - Cancelling a download no longer polls GET_DEVICE_STATUS (some phones never
    answer it and stop responding) and sends the cancel request only once.
  - Two small memory leaks fixed in LIBMTP_Set_Object_Filename.
  - A failed open (e.g. the USB interface is claimed by another process) now
    closes the USB device handle instead of leaking it.
  - Android devices are no longer USB-reset when a session closes (the reset
    makes many phones drop out of File transfer mode).
  - When opening a session fails, the retry skips its USB reset for devices
    flagged DEVICE_FLAG_NO_USB_RESET.

Build: MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=11.0 CFLAGS="-arch arm64 -O2" LDFLAGS="-arch arm64"
./configure --disable-static --disable-mtpz --with-udev=no (libmtp); libusb is
configured the same way plus ac_cv_func_pipe2=no.
